summary: Daniel M. Stuart works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (~2006–2012) under Alexander von Rospatt and became Assistant Professor of South Asian and Buddhist Studies at the University of South Carolina around 2013.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a thesis at Florida State University (~2010–2012) under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Stuart Capper, Jr. specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. He completed a BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993–2000).

Daniel Veidlinger is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1996–2002) under Steven Collins. He served as a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999) and joined California State University, Chico (~2004).

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia. He has held instructor positions at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.

Daniel Walker Howe (1937–2025) was a historian of religion. He studied at Harvard, Magdalen College, Oxford, and UC Berkeley before serving as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from ~1973 to 1992.

Daniela Berti specializes in Indology and ethno-anthropology. She earned her PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology from the University of Siena and served as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed her PhD jointly at Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University (~2011–2015) and served as a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London (2015–2020).
Daniele Cuneo is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Arinde L. Jonker. Around 2016, he held a post at the University of Paris.
Danielle Feller specializes in Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (~1996–2001) under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst.

Daoquan Yu (1901–1992) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1934–1937). In 1950, he became professor of Tibetan Language and literature at Minzu University of China.

Daud Ali is a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at William & Mary (~1982–1986) and the University of Chicago (~1989–1996), and held posts at SOAS University of London (~1995–2009) and the University of Pennsylvania (~2009).
David A. Dilworth is a scholar of philosophy and Japanology who studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo. He held an academic post at Stony Brook University from ~1970 to 2005.

David A. Hall specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology, earning a doctorate at the University of California, Berkeley (-1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and served as Chair of Science, Engineering and Technology at Montgomery College.
David Azzopardi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (-2010) under the supervision of Kate Crosby.

David B. Gray works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Columbia (~1995–2001) under Robert A. F. Thurman, held a fellowship at Rice (~2001–2003), and became an associate professor at Santa Clara University (~2005).

David Bubna-Litic works in Buddhist studies and business management. He earned his PhD from Western Sydney University and served as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney.

David Burton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at the University of Bristol (1994–1997) under Paul Williams. Around 2001, he became a Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University.

David Drewes specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from Lawrence and Virginia, where he studied under Karen C. Lang. He taught at Virginia and Indiana University before joining the University of Manitoba as Assistant Professor around 2008.
David E. Cooper is a philosopher who attended Highgate School and served as Professor of Philosophy at Durham University from 1986 to 2009.
